head: 1b774fb6cac181bb8d7a6739f5a81914f99b941c
issue:
Back-to-back bookings are treated as double-booked

A booking that ends at 10:00 and the next one that starts at 10:00 do not share any time, but the booking helpers treat them as a clash. Example with times in minutes since midnight:

    find_conflicts([(540, 600), (600, 660)])   # returns [((540, 600), (600, 660))], should be []
    merge_bookings([(540, 600), (600, 660)])   # returns [(540, 660)], should stay [(540, 600), (600, 660)]

Back-to-back bookings must not be reported as conflicts and must not be merged into one block. Bookings that really overlap (for example (540, 600) and (570, 630)) must keep behaving as before.

triage.text:
REPRODUCES
The test failure confirms the reported bug: merge_bookings incorrectly merges back-to-back intervals into a single block.

import pytest

def test_back_to_back_bookings():
    from bookings import overlaps, find_conflicts, merge_bookings

    # Overlapping bookings should still be detected
    assert overlaps((540, 600), (570, 630))
    # Disjoint bookings should not clash
    assert not overlaps((540, 600), (700, 760))
    # Back-to-back bookings must not be considered overlapping
    assert not overlaps((540, 600), (600, 660))

    # find_conflicts should not report back-to-back as a conflict
    assert find_conflicts([(540, 600), (600, 660)]) == []
    # But should still report real overlaps
    assert find_conflicts([(540, 600), (570, 630), (800, 860)]) == [((540, 600), (570, 630))]

    # merge_bookings must not merge back-to-back bookings
    assert merge_bookings([(540, 600), (600, 660)]) == [(540, 600), (600, 660)]
    # But should still merge truly overlapping bookings
    assert merge_bookings([(540, 600), (570, 630), (800, 860)]) == [(540, 630), (800, 860)]
